The calendar includes professional development days, conference exchange days, and various holidays throughout the year.

item.title: Community BINGO for Older Americans Month
item.description:
May is Older Americans Month with the 2026 theme "Champion Your Health". Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community are hosting Community BINGO throughout May. Pick up BINGO cards at Oxford Seniors (922 Tollgate Dr.), Oxford Lane Library (441 S. Locust St.), The Knolls of Oxford, or Scripps Gerontology Center (396 Upham Hall). Complete activities on the card to mark off squares, then bring your completed card to an Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sunday, May 31 from 3:00-5:00 PM at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and fun.

item.title: School Medication Policy and Pickup Procedures
item.description:
Students cannot transport any medications (prescription or over-the-counter) to or from school - an adult must pick up all medications. If your child needs medication at school, contact Nurse Tonja to arrange pickup. The notice includes an illustration of medication bottles and pills to emphasize this important safety policy.

item.title: Summer Reading Tips to Prevent Learning Loss
item.description:
As the school year ends, families are encouraged to prevent "summer slide" (learning loss over summer break) by keeping students reading. Resources include Lane Library, the Bookmobile (library card needed), free e-books at HooplaDigital.com, and Little Free Libraries at elementary schools. Activity ideas include creating cozy reading spaces, building blanket forts for reading adventures, and participating in Scholastic's Summer Reading Bingo. Parents are reminded they are their child's best teacher.

item.title: May 2026 Breakfast and Lunch Menus
item.description:
Marshall Elementary's May 2026 breakfast and lunch menus are now available. School is not in session May 4-5 (no school). The final day with meals is May 22, followed by Memorial Day on May 25. School's out for summer starting May 26-29. All breakfasts include 100% fruit juice, fresh fruit selection, and choice of milk. All lunches include choice of milk. Menu items include various breakfast options like donuts, pancake bites, and waffles, plus lunch items such as pizza, hot dogs, chicken tenders, and corn dogs with accompanying sides and fruits.

item.title: Oxford Lions Club Eyeglasses Donation Drive
item.description:
The Oxford Lions Club Sight Saving Committee is collecting used eyeglasses, sunglasses, and cases to donate to children in need worldwide. The lenses and frames are modified to meet individual children's eye needs, with 900+ pairs sent annually.

Donations can be sent to Betsy Beaton at Marshall Elementary School or Shaunna Tafelski at the Board Office by mid-May. The committee can pick up donations or items can be dropped off at either location.

item.title: Oxford Swim and Dive Team Registration
item.description:
The Oxford Swim and Dive Team is a community-oriented summer competitive team for ages 4-18 of all abilities. Practices begin May 26, 2026 at the Oxford Aquatic Center. Costs are $150 (swim), $120 (dive), or $200 (both), with family discounts available. A trial period runs May 26-29 for $30, ending with a mock meet. Register at swimosdt.com or contact oxfordswimdive@gmail.com. Coach Steve also offers a Makos Stroke Clinic for ages 5-13 at Miami's Rec Center (April 20 - May 22, 2026, Mon/Wed/Fri 5:30-6:30 PM, $180).

item.title: Marshall Mile & Family Picnic Event
item.description:
The Marshall Mile and Family Picnic takes place Friday, May 8th with different times for each grade. Students should come without backpacks. The mile run will be in the parking lot, followed by a family picnic on the playground by the swing set. Families can bring picnic lunches or students can purchase lunch in the cafeteria. Sign-out will be at the door nearest the swing set with a green slip system. Schedule: Grades 1-2 run at 11:15-11:25 with picnic 11:45-12:35, Grades K-3 run at 12:10-12:20 with picnic 12:40-1:30, Grades 4-5 run at 1:05-1:20 with picnic 1:40-2:30.

item.title: Tips for Improving Student Reading Comprehension
item.description:
Parents can help assess reading comprehension by asking questions about story elements like characters, setting, and plot. Suggested activities: have students retell the story or draw pictures about what they read. The Reading Corner program uses the UFLI curriculum and offers a parent resource guide. Contact your student's Reading Corner teacher for additional support.

item.title: Welcome Back and State Testing Underway
item.description:
Welcome back from Spring Break! Students returned with great energy and focus after the break. State testing has begun and students are showing excellent effort and perseverance.
